title: Hardship Assistance Programs Terms: Fee Relief at Activation and Leaving a Plan Early
content:
## When a plan becomes active

When a plan of the Hardship Assistance Programs becomes active:

- late and returned-payment fees on the loan assessed within the program's fee waiver look-back before the request date and still unpaid are waived as hardship relief (Servicemember and Disaster Relief fees follow their own rules);
- collection contact stops where the program says so;
- the loan is reported to the credit bureaus as the program's credit reporting treatment states.

While the plan is active, late fees are suspended on installments falling due under it where the program suspends them.

*Hypothetical, a 30-day look-back:* an unpaid late fee assessed 10 days before the request date is waived when the plan becomes active; one assessed 45 days before it is not waived under this rule; a fee already paid is not waived.

## Leaving a plan early

A borrower may leave an active plan at any time. The plan closes as cancelled, the loan's original rate and installment resume from the next due date, deferred installments already moved stay moved, and fees already waived stay waived. Leaving a Term Extension Modification before its trial ends means the modification never takes effect.

| On leaving an active plan | Result |
|---|---|
| Plan status | cancelled |
| Rate and installment | the loan's original ones resume from the next due date |
| Installments already deferred | stay moved |
| Fees already waived | stay waived |
| Term Extension Modification still in trial | the modification never takes effect |

The look-back, late-fee suspension, collection, reporting and AutoPay treatment of each program are given in the account treatment matrix.
